entries.title: Answer quiz questions in the margin
entries.body: In Marginalia, pressing a quiz question opens a small box beneath it where you can type your answer, and the feedback appears in the margin as it is written. Each question has a microphone button that opens the box and starts dictation in one press. A question you have answered gets a pale green background and a tick, in the margin and in Learn's quiz alike; green means answered, not right.

entries.title: Explained passages are underlined in the text
entries.body: Passages the Explanations mode has explained get a dotted teal underline in the article, in every mode. Point at or tap one to see its explanation, with buttons to ask about it in chat or open it in Explanations. This is behind the Experimental features switch on your profile page.

entries.title: Articles reopen where you left off, anywhere
entries.body: Opening a half-read article in a browser that had never shown it before started at the top, with the guide meant for a first visit. Now it opens at the paragraph you last read on another device. A browser that already remembers your place in that article still goes back there.

entries.title: Tapping a comment over a glossary term works
entries.body: On a phone or tablet, tapping a comment or chat that covered a glossary term or a citation showed the term's card instead of opening your comment or chat. It opens the comment or chat. Passages with a chat attached also show a pointing-hand cursor.
